summary: The article surveys how regional orchards and vineyards inspire homemade fruit-infused specialties as summer turns to autumn 2023. It covers grape sauces and preserves, applesauce, canned peaches, berries and cream, fruit cocktails, fruit vinegars and cheese pairings, with quotes from local growers, chefs and instructors. It closes on the sustainability and community ties between producers and consumers.
one_line: A seasonal guide to turning orchard and vineyard fruits into homemade sauces, preserves, cocktails, vinegars and pairings, with local expert voices.
key_facts: As of September 1st, 2023, local communities showed increased interest in homegrown produce and traditional culinary practices.
Charlotte Green of Green's Family Orchard said on September 15th that fruits are chosen 'for their stories and flavors'.
Grape varieties are harvested in late September and early October and selected for compatibility with specific dishes.
Oliver Martinez, head winemaker at Bella Vida Vineyard, said on October 5th that grapes can become sauces, syrups or marinades.
Lucia Bertolli, an artisanal food crafter, infuses her Italian heritage into her grape preserves sold at farmer's markets.
Ethan Parker, food blogger and culinary instructor, said at a November 2nd apple preservation workshop that homemade applesauce unlocks new flavors with each apple variety.
Patricia Smith of Smithfield Orchards called peach preservation 'a love letter to summer'; peaches can be made into syrups, chutneys and savory salsa.
Pastry chef Thomas Keller revealed the berries-and-cream pairing at a berry festival on September 24th; it uses sugar and a dash of vanilla.
Miranda Lee, bar owner and cocktail expert, spoke at the regional cocktail fair on September 30th about the fruit-infused cocktail boom.
Fermentation specialist Daniel Roth leads vinegar workshops on making fruit-based vinegars by naturally fermenting fruit juices.
At the Harvest Pairings event on October 10th, Sophia Nguyen demonstrated cheese boards; Granny Smith apples pair with sharp cheddar.
The article ends by noting sustainability, community-supported agriculture, farm-to-table restaurants and local food movements.
